stories.headline: Inside the tension, suspicion and history behind Amanda Nunes vs. Kayla Harrison
stories.summary: Kayla Harrison thought she had found a teammate, but Amanda Nunes saw a future rival. What really happened?
stories.body:
In their own ways, Amanda Nunes and Kayla Harrison both waited a very long time for what happened on June 7, 2025.

On that evening in Newark, New Jersey, Harrison submitted Julianna Peña to become UFC bantamweight champion. Nunes, who retired in 2023, was in attendance and eager to make a return to fight Harrison, with whom she shares a complicated past. The UFC allowed Nunes to enter the Octagon immediately after Harrison's win, so the two could square off on the spot.

That single encounter represented something Harrison had worked for her entire career: an opportunity to test herself against the very best. And even after two years away from competition, Nunes, considered the best women fighter in UFC history, remained that gold standard.

For Nunes, it was something else: a chance to expose a suspicion she'd held about Harrison for many years.

"I asked her, 'You planned this the whole time, right?'" Nunes told ESPN in January. "I wanted everybody to hear it from her own mouth. This is what was happening the whole time. You planned this."

Looking back, Harrison says she didn't understand at that moment the point Nunes was trying to make. The scene was chaotic. She had just fought, won a championship and was suddenly promoting her next fight. She managed to offer Nunes a simple response, "Let's do it," and only later understood the accusation being made.

"It didn't really sink in until I watched it later, and I was like, 'Oh, she really thinks I have been scheming this since the beginning," Harrison told ESPN on Nov. 3. "And to be fair, that would be a s---ty feeling. To think this whole time, your own team and coaches plotted against you. That is a terrible feeling that I can't even imagine.

"But it's just not true."

On Saturday, Harrison (19-1) and Nunes (23-5) will finally meet for the 135-pound championship at UFC 334 at New York's Madison Square Garden (Paramount, 9 p.m. ET), in one of the biggest fights in women's MMA history. Harrison is a two-time Olympic judo gold medalist and one of the most decorated combat sports athletes ever. Nunes is an icon of women's MMA, its greatest of all time. A two-division champion who overwhelmed such fighters as Ronda Rousey, Cris Cyborg and Holly Holm during her generational run at the top.

If that weren't enough, Harrison and Nunes have a history. They spent several years training at American Top Team in Coconut Creek, Florida. Harrison joined the gym in 2018, at the beginning of her MMA career. Nunes, who was already the UFC's dominant champion when Harrison arrived, left the gym in 2022, and eventually identified Harrison as her reason for leaving. In the time since, Nunes has accused Harrison -- and even others at American Top Team -- of planning this fight from the very beginning.

What unfolded between them could be described as deceit, misunderstanding or paranoia -- depending on who you ask. Both, Harrison and Nunes say that whatever the case, there's no animosity going into UFC 334. American Top Team owner Dan Lambert, for one, doesn't believe that.

"It's a hell of a story, and there's more between these two than they'll ever let us know," Lambert told ESPN in January. "They'll say all the right things about each other. But my opinion? They probably hate each other's f---ing guts is my opinion."

When Harrison first arrived at American Top Team, she was looking for a place to build her MMA career with others. She had spent her entire life in judo, and understood that reaching the highest level of even an individual sport, still requires a team. Including training partners.

She visited MMA gyms in New Jersey and Las Vegas before making her way to South Florida, where she instantly clicked with the coaches, the lifestyle and -- she thought -- one of the gym's prized athletes. Nunes.

"When I first met Amanda, she was like, 'Hey, you need to come here, it's great, I'd love to have you in camp,'" Harrison said. "And I was like, 'Oh, absolutely.' She seemed nice."

They sparred that week. Harrison was just starting out, and she remembers walking away from the session covered in bruises. They sparred only two rounds, Harrison said, but spending that time with Nunes felt good. Shortly after, she made a full commitment to American Top Team.

"It pisses me off thinking about it now, because I moved here with the expectation that we were going to be in it together," Harrison said. "I moved here thinking, 'Oh s---, we're about to level the f--- up. It's going to be me and her. And then obviously it ended up very different."

That expectation came from Harrison's experience in judo, where, she said, athletes regularly train with -- and then compete against -- each other. Harrison has memories of traveling through Hungary, Croatia and France, where she would work with women she might eventually face in the Olympics. For Harrison, there's no contradiction in that arrangement. Train together, improve together, and compete against each other if and when the time comes. She said she applies that mindset to her training now as a UFC champion, routinely welcoming and rolling with other bantamweights, including No. 15-ranked Bia Mesquita, at American Top Team.

"I don't have a scarcity mindset," Harrison said. "I don't think that for me to win, you have to lose. I think we all have our time and place and rising tides raise all ships."

Nunes views things differently.

She said she initially welcomed Harrison, but immediately picked up an energy that was different from regular work. Harrison wasn't there simply to innocently train alongside her. She was there to ultimately challenge Nunes in every sense of the word.

"I'm the kind of fighter who visualizes the future," Nunes said. "And from the first time I trained with Kayla, I told [my wife and then-UFC strawweight] Nina, 'I am going to fight this girl.' The first time we exchanged, I looked at Nina and said, 'This girl is different.'"

After that first spar, the two rarely worked together again. On this matter, at least, everyone agrees.

"How many rounds of sparring, real sparring, between them? Less than 10," American Top Team coach Mike Brown told ESPN in January. "Kayla always wanted to train with Amanda, but Amanda never wanted to train with her."

Nunes says she never interfered with Harrison's desire to join the gym and actually believes it was probably the right move for her career. But she maintains that Harrison should have been honest with Nunes, the coaches -- and herself -- on her reasons. "She didn't do anything wrong, wanting to come after me," Nunes said. "My life is all about the challenge. I love the challenge. I like that when you look at me, you want what I have. Let's go.

"But own it."

To be fair, in a very real way, Harrison did own it.

In 2018, before she'd even competed in MMA, she was already fielding questions about UFC titles, Nunes, Rousey and every other significant name at the top of the sport because of her undeniable potential as an Olympic gold medalist. And in all those interviews, she always said if the moment came that the challenge was Nunes, she would welcome it. That's what competitors do.

Nunes and those closest to her, however, saw it as one and the same. If Harrison's target was to be the best, and Nunes was the best -- then Nunes was the target. And there are certain realities to that in MMA.

"People talk like it's a high school wrestling tournament where you're like, 'Oh, I'm so happy for you,'" Nina Nunes told ESPN in January. "No. This is food in my kid's mouth. It's my kid's education. It's my legacy, forever. These are things that are very personal. It's fine if others don't see it that way. We see it that way."

In spite of the fundamental differences in which each viewed Harrison's presence in the gym, it managed to work for several years. Harrison signed with the PFL, and became the face of that MMA promotion. She won multiple tournaments, and twice signed exclusive contracts that prevented her from considering the UFC. The two champions of different organizations shared a facility and even coaches with one another, but did not cross paths -- in professional competition or even in training.

That all worked relatively well until December 2021.

On Dec. 11, 2021, Nunes was scheduled to make the sixth defense of her bantamweight championship against Peña at UFC 269 in Las Vegas.

Two months prior, Harrison had won her second lightweight championship in the PFL, and wrapped up her exclusive contract with the promotion. She began a period of free agency, in which she could field offers from other organizations, but the PFL maintained its right to match any in order to keep her in its roster.

Harrison, who had already fought four times in 2021 and was essentially out of the gym on holiday, flew to Las Vegas to watch her teammate, Nunes, defend her title.

"So, this is where it got a little weird," Brown said. "And you have to ask Dan [Lambert] about this, because he knows more about it than I do. But Amanda thought the UFC had plans that when she won, Kayla was going to get into the ring to challenge her. She believed there was some conspiracy to announce that fight."

When asked for his recollection of that event, Lambert gives a knowing smile but refuses to go into detail.

"I have a rule of never divulging s--- about what happens in the gym," Lambert says. "You have to ask Amanda. I'm not going to say what Amanda thought or what Amanda said, but one million percent, Kayla was not going to the UFC.

"I can even tell you that Kayla and her manager went to dinner with [UFC chief business officer] Hunter Campbell that week, and I told Hunter, 'No matter what happens at this dinner, no matter what happens at this dinner, I will kill [any potential deal]. I guarantee you, she is not going to the UFC [to fight].' I knew it would be a problem for Amanda, and there were other options for Kayla. There was an opportunity for Kayla to go make a bunch of money in Bellator MMA or PFL, and then go to the UFC a year later. That was my plan."

From Nunes and her family's perspective, all of it -- Harrison's backstage presence during fight week, her dinner with a UFC executive, an interview in which UFC CEO Dana White publicly confirmed his personal interest in Harrison -- was proof of what she'd felt, clearly, from Day 1.

She was always going to fight Kayla Harrison, and Kayla Harrison had always intended for it to happen.

"It was the biggest 'duh' moment of all time," Nina Nunes said. She's a free agent. She's having dinner with the UFC. She's sitting in the front row.

As much as they want to say, 'No, it's not what you think,' how could anyone think it was anything else? We didn't know if the UFC would bring Kayla into the ring, but we felt she was there for a reason."

At UFC 269 inside T-Mobile Arena, Nunes suffered one of the biggest upsets in UFC title fight history. As a more than 11-to-1 betting favorite, Nunes surrendered her bantamweight championship to Peña, tapping to a rear-naked choke at 3:26 of the second round.

Whether any of Nunes's performance that night can be tied to what happened behind the scenes is speculative. She has never publicly blamed American Top Team for the loss, which is her only defeat in 12 UFC championship fights. But by the time Nunes drove back to Florida from Las Vegas (she and Nina drive to the majority of her fights), she'd already decided to leave the gym and open her own facility in South Florida. Just like that, the 10-year relationship between Nunes and American Top Team, which had produced the greatest run in women's MMA history, was over.

Harrison found out secondhand.

"I was shocked," she said. "I had sent her a text when she lost, 'Let's get back in the gym and get this back,' and she'd responded something like, 'Thank you, cutie,' or whatever. And then the next thing you know, she was leaving.

"I couldn't understand it, because I've lost before, and it was on me. It wasn't on the coaches. The game plan wasn't flawed. I lost because I lost. And I felt that way about Amanda. She got in her own head that night. And that's on her."

The physical UFC belt that Nunes won for dethroning Cris Cyborg in December 2018 to become the only women's double champ is still displayed in the front lobby of American Top Team gym. But every photo of Nunes that once hung on the walls or rafters has been removed.

Lambert says he's long given up trying to make sense of athletes who come and go from his gym, but he won't celebrate them once they're gone.

"You're either with us or you're not," Lambert said. "You'll see pictures of [retired lightweight] Cole Miller up there with his American Top Team tattoos long after I die. But people who leave the gym? No.

"I'll keep her belt there, because that's testimony to what we did as a team, when we were together. I'm not putting a picture up and celebrating someone who didn't want to be here anymore."

Is the environment of American Top Team itself at fault for any of what happened between Nunes and Harrison?

Brown acknowledges that filling a practice mat with UFC contenders from the same weight class -- something that happens occasionally -- may not be the ideal training environment. As a coach, he encourages his athletes to push themselves, while also making their teammates improve. But he understand the potential conflict that approaches create.

"You don't want to be helping the guy next to you, giving him your secrets and your tricks, if you think he might be a future opponent," Brown said. "You're going to be selfish and keep everything to yourself. So, as a coach, I don't like the idea of pooling guys who might fight each other."

Lambert agrees, but doesn't see an alternative. As the gym's owner, his doors have always been open to the best talent in the world. There are certain realities that come with that, and it's up to the individual athletes to figure out what they're comfortable with.

"I've had issues where people at our gym have said, 'Hey, I don't want other people in my weight class in the gym,'" Lambert says. "And my response is always the same. 'How the f--- am I going to run a gym with one person in every weight class?' I could do that out of my garage. I want a gym that is full of killers in every weight class, because we think that's how people get better and get pushed between camps. We've had situations where teammates have had to fight. Sometimes they deal with it well, and sometimes they don't."

Both Nunes and Harrison adamantly deny Lambert's suggestion that they "hate each other's guts." They simply don't understand each other.

Nunes will never understand how Harrison and the team turned a blind eye to what she said was obvious from the very beginning. Harrison walked into her gym and challenged her place in the sport. She wasn't just open to the possibility of fighting Nunes, she wanted it. And eight years after they first met, the fight is finally happening. In Nunes' eyes, this was always the final destination, and she doesn't appreciate anyone -- least of all, Harrison -- who pretended otherwise.

Harrison, meanwhile, will never understand Nunes's lack of interest in what she initially offered: a teammate. Someone to push her, challenge her, and ultimately make her better. Harrison didn't go to Florida to take Nunes down, she said. She went to Florida so they could each become the best versions of themselves.

"Maybe the writing was on the wall for everyone, and I sound like the dumb blonde who didn't know we would eventually fight," Harrison says. "But she wasn't my goal. Of course, I wanted to get to the point where I was good enough to challenge her, but I was also just learning on the job and figuring things out."

They might never see the events of the last eight years the same way. But on Saturday in New York, they will settle the one question that might have been at the center all this time: Who is the best?

stories.headline: NBA Power Rankings: 1-30 poll, plus the best newcomer on all 30 teams
stories.summary: Which NBA teams rise and which fall in this week's Power Rankings? Plus, the top newcomer for each team in the league.
stories.body:
The NBA season is starting to take shape as the holiday window approaches.

The San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder are once again surging early, but their Western Conference counterparts the Los Angeles Lakers have arguably been the most impressive team in a competitive West. The Lakers are fueled by Luka Doncic's historic start, which has featured 39.3 points, 7.8 rebounds and 7.7 assists per game.

In the East, the new look Philadelphia 76ers seem like they've been playing together for years, as LeBron James and Jaylen Brown have hit the ground running with their new teammates. They're tailed tightly by their offseason trade partners, the Boston Celtics, who seemingly haven't missed a beat with new faces around Jayson Tatum.

In this week's Power Rankings, our ESPN Insiders rank where each team stands, per usual, and also highlight each team's best newcomer over the first few weeks of the season. Which players are vaulting their teams up the standings? Find out in this week's Power Rankings.

Previous rankings: Preseason | Oct. 28 | Nov. 4

Jump to a team:

ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE

DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND

LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN

NO | NY | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX

POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS

1. San Antonio Spurs

2026-27 record: 9-2
Previous ranking: 5
Next games: @ CHI (Nov. 11), vs. GS (Nov. 13), @ UTAH (Nov. 15)

Top newcomer: C Tarris Reed Jr.

Drafted 26th in 2026, Tarris Reed Jr. knew earning minutes as a rookie in San Antonio would be difficult, even after he gave French phenom Victor Wembanyama buckets, according to sources, in the early days of open gym over the summer. Reed is averaging just 5.3 minutes per game, but the Spurs' brass has been impressed with the rookie's preparedness every time his number is called. San Antonio is thin at center, and veteran backup Luke Kornet has struggled. That could lead to more minutes for Reed as the season progresses. -- Mike C. Wright

2. Los Angeles Lakers

2026-27 record: 10-2
Previous ranking: 7
Next games: @ MIL (Nov. 11), @ PHX (Nov. 15), vs. CHA (Nov. 17)

Top newcomer: C Walker Kessler

After recording one of the most memorable debuts imaginable -- when he scored 26 points on a perfect 12-for-12 from the field in a win -- Kessler has continued to have a major impact. The 7-2 center has been durable, playing in all 12 of L.A.'s games, and averaging a career high in points (14.9) while shooting 69.1% from the field, with 10.8 rebounds and 2.3 blocks per game. He has also played north of 30 minutes per game while only averaging 2.9 fouls, which is paramount for a Lakers roster without a go-to big man to back him up. -- Dave McMenamin

3. Oklahoma City Thunder

2026-27 record: 8-3
Previous ranking: 10
Next games: @ POR (Nov. 11), @ LAC (Nov. 13), @ SAC (Nov. 15)

Top newcomer: C Aday Mara

Rookie center Aday Mara, selected with the No. 12 pick courtesy of the LA Clippers, has made an instant impact in Oklahoma City. The 7-foot-3 big man entered the league as an elite rim protector, ranking fifth in the NBA with 1.9 blocks per game. Mara also has soft touch in the paint and has intriguing potential as a passer. He ranks fifth among rookies in rebounding (5.9 per game) and is also averaging 8.1 points on 62.5% shooting over 19 minutes per game. -- Tim MacMahon

4. Philadelphia 76ers

2026-27 record: 9-3
Previous ranking: 3
Next games: vs. TOR (Nov. 12), vs. IND (Nov. 15), @ BKN (Nov. 16)

Top newcomer: G Jaylen Brown

Brown has said that this is Tyrese Maxey's team, but as of late, it's starting to look like his, as well. He had his best stretch as a Sixer on the team's recent road trip, scoring 30-points in a win over Detroit and 29 points in a win over the Chicago Bulls.

"He's something we really needed," Maxey said. -- Kris Rhim

5. Boston Celtics

2026-27 record: 9-2
Previous ranking: 4
Next games: @ TOR (Nov. 11), vs. DAL (Nov. 15), vs. ORL (Nov. 16)

Top newcomer: F Paul George

George set the tone for what this season would be on opening night, breaking the franchise record for the most points in a debut with 38. Since then, he has remained a seamless fit in Boston, becoming one of the team's best wing defenders and a reliable second option on offense as the Celtics have jumped out to the second-best record in the East.

"On and off the court he's been great," coach Joe Mazzulla said. -- Rhim

6. Minnesota Timberwolves

2026-27 record: 8-3
Previous ranking: 11
Next games: vs. DAL (Nov. 12), vs. CHI (Nov. 14), vs. POR (Nov. 16)

Top newcomer: G LaMelo Ball

The Timberwolves should be ecstatic with the early returns from their summer trade for Ball, who quickly forged a dynamic partnership with Anthony Edwards. Even after Edwards was sidelined by knee surgery, Ball has kept Minnesota's offense in the top 10 and is on pace to be the franchise's first player to average at least six assists since D'Angelo Russell in 2022-23. Meanwhile, the Hornets' offensive efficiency has plummeted from fifth last season to 30th this season after trading Ball in June. No takebacks. -- Ben Golliver

7. Houston Rockets

2026-27 record: 8-3
Previous ranking: 1
Next games: vs. GS (Nov. 11), vs. UTAH (Nov. 13), @ WAS (Nov. 15)

Top newcomer: G Marcus Smart

Veteran guard Marcus Smart is not only reliable for coach Ime Udoka but also familiar with him from their time together with the Celtics. Most of all, Smart gives the Rockets another steady ball handler and tenacious defender capable of starting whenever Fred VanVleet is forced to rest on the second night of back-to-backs, as he continues to recover from last year's ACL surgery. A former NBA Defensive Player of the Year, Smart plays with the intelligence and toughness that Udoka covets and provides veteran leadership alongside VanVleet and Kevin Durant. -- Mike C. Wright

8. Detroit Pistons

2026-27 record: 7-3
Previous ranking: 2
Next games: @ WAS (Nov. 12), @ MIA (Nov. 14), @ SAS (Nov. 17)

Top newcomer: F John Collins

It was a bit of a slow start for Collins, who signed as a free agent to replace veteran Tobias Harris. Collins fits more what the Pistons want to be, with his athleticism and shooting as complements to Jalen Duren's interior presence. However, with Duren out with a hamstring injury, it forced Collins to be paired with Paul Reed, which has been a bit clunky. When J.B. Bickerstaff removed Reed from the first five and went small against the Wizards, it opened things up for Collins -- he scored a season-high 24 points and added 10 rebounds in a 122-111 win Monday night. -- Vince Goodwill

9. Golden State Warriors

2026-27 record: 8-3
Previous ranking: 12
Next games: @ HOU (Nov. 11), @ SAS (Nov. 13), @ NO (Nov. 16)

Top newcomer: F Yaxel Lendeborg

During one of his unfiltered livestreams this summer, Lendeborg -- the outspoken No. 11 pick -- predicted he would average around 15 points, six rebounds and four assists as a rookie. It felt overly ambitious at the time. It appears he might've been shorting himself. Through his first 11 games, Lendeborg is averaging 21.4 points, 7.2 rebounds and four assists. The scoring punch has been particularly surprising and important for the surging 8-3 Warriors. Lendeborg is making better than 44% of his 5.5 attempted 3s per game and has gained enough trust from Steve Kerr that he is putting the basketball in the rookie's hands to make decisions down the stretch of close games. -- Anthony Slater

10. New York Knicks

2026-27 record: 6-4
Previous ranking: 17
Next games: vs. CLE (Nov. 11), @ IND (Nov. 13), @ TOR (Nov. 15)

Top newcomer: C Andre Drummond

At times it has appeared like Drummond has been out of place, with Mike Brown pulling Drummond abruptly in the middle of games for not getting back on defense and trying his hand with James Wiseman instead. But one thing that cannot be denied is Drummond's effect on the glass. The Knicks were supposed to suffer a drop-off as one of the best offensive rebounding teams after Mitchell Robinson departed to Boston. But per 36 minutes, Drummond has averaged over eight offensive rebounds to help the Knicks remain a top-three team in that category. And Brown has complemented Drummond's screen-roll defense recently, noting his physicality. -- Vince Goodwill

11. Portland Trail Blazers

2026-27 record: 7-3
Previous ranking: 8
Next games: vs. OKC (Nov. 11), @ SAC (Nov. 13), @ MIN (Nov. 16)

Top newcomer: G Damian Lillard

Portland's best newcomer is actually an old friend in Lillard, who is doing his best to make Rip City forget that he was traded to the Bucks in 2023 and missed last season with an Achilles injury. Lillard, 36, is averaging 19.4 points and 4.4 assists, and he has made fast friends with All-Star wing Deni Avdija. The Blazers boast an excellent plus-9.4 net rating when Avdija and Lillard, their two leading scorers, share the court. -- Ben Golliver

12. Denver Nuggets

2026-27 record: 5-4
Previous ranking: 15
Next games: @ MEM (Nov. 11), @ NO (Nov. 14), vs. PHX (Nov. 16)

Top newcomer: F Trevon Brazile

The Nuggets remain in a perpetual search for lineup combinations that can survive in the minutes either Nikola Jokic or the scorching Jamal Murray are off the floor. Through nine games, they're minus-15 in Jokic's bench time and minus-29 in Murray's. But within that, in their latest search for depth pieces after Peyton Watson's departure this past summer, they've received encouraging contributions from Trevon Brazile and Bryce Hopkins -- both second-rounders from the 2026 draft. Brazile is a 6-10 wing with a 7-4 wingspan, flashing early as a rebounder and a defensive disruptor in a few of Denver's wins. He's averaging 20.3 minutes, a number that might rise as the season progresses. -- Slater

13. Memphis Grizzlies

2026-27 record: 7-3
Previous ranking: 6
Next games: vs. DEN (Nov. 11), @ NO (Nov. 13), vs. @BKN (Nov. 14)

Top newcomer: F Cameron Boozer

Rookie Cameron Boozer, the third pick of the 2026 draft, is already surprising some opponents with his unexpected agility and scoring prowess. "I had no clue he could move the way he moves, also that he could shoot the way he shoots," said Golden State center Draymond Green on "The Draymond Green Show" podcast. With Isaiah Stewart out due to a right knee bone bruise, Boozer is also having to showcase his versatility by sliding over from his natural power forward spot to center.

"We are featuring him in a lot of different sets," Grizzlies coach Tuomas Iisalo said. -- Wright

14. Atlanta Hawks

2026-27 record: 7-5
Previous ranking: 18
Next games: @ CHI (Nov. 13), @ MIL (Nov. 15)

Top newcomer: G Kingston Flemings

With the Hawks' offense struggling early in the season, coach Quin Snyder inserted the rookie Flemings into the starting lineup and moved veteran CJ McCollum to a reserve role. The Hawks went on to win three out of the four games with Flemings as starter while ranking fifth in offense. Something to pay attention to is whether Snyder trusts Flemings to close games. In the last four games, he ranks eighth in minutes per game in the fourth quarter. -- Bobby Marks

15. Dallas Mavericks

2026-27 record: 7-4
Previous ranking: 13
Next games: @ MIN (Nov. 12), @ CLE (Nov. 14), @ BOS (Nov. 15)

Top newcomer: G Zaccharie Risacher

The Mavericks took a flyer on Risacher when they acquired him in the three-way trade that sent Luguentz Dort to Atlanta, hoping they could develop the former No. 1 pick into a quality role player. The 6-9 Risacher has impressed with his defensive activity as a reserve, averaging 1.3 steals and 1.1 blocks per game. Coach Dusty May is comfortable giving Risacher the assignment of guarding elite scorers across multiple positions. His defense on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Kevin Durant helped the Mavs pull off wins over the Thunder and Rockets. -- MacMahon

16. Cleveland Cavaliers

2026-27 record: 5-6
Previous ranking: 9
Next games: @ NYK (Nov. 11), @ MIA (Nov. 13), vs. DAL (Nov. 14)

Top newcomer: G Meleek Thomas

Headline acquisition Peyton Watson is still struggling to find his footing in Cleveland, but Thomas, picked 34th in the 2026 draft, has been a pleasant surprise for the Cavaliers. The rookie guard shone at summer league and has carried over that performance to games that count, averaging 13 points and hitting 48% of his 3s so far. After starting the season with three DNPs in Cleveland's first five games, Thomas has quickly worked his way into playing 20-plus minutes every night. -- Zach Kram

17. Toronto Raptors

2026-27 record: 5-5
Previous ranking: 14
Next games: vs. BOS (Nov. 11), @ PHI (Nov. 12), vs. NYK (Nov. 15)

Top newcomer: F Allen Graves

This should be going to Kawhi Leonard, who returned to Toronto in an offseason trade, but he has only played two games this season while sidelined with soreness in his left knee. The reality for the Raptors is that no newcomer has made a significant impact this season, but Graves, the team's first-round pick, has been the best of the team's additions, which includes veteran Kyle Anderson and rookie Jaden Bradley. He has reached double digits once this season, scoring 11 points in a loss to Minnesota, and has largely played a depth role. -- Rhim

18. Miami Heat

2026-27 record: 5-6
Previous ranking: 19
Next games: vs. CLE (Nov. 13), vs. DET (Nov. 14), vs. HOU (Nov. 16)

Top newcomer: F Giannis Antetokounmpo

Even with the Heat's early season struggles, it would be almost malpractice if we left Antetokounmpo off the list. After playing a career-low 36 games last season with Milwaukee, Antetokounmpo has appeared in all 10 games this season. The former MVP has scored 25 points or more in seven games and is on pace to average the most rebounds in his career since 2019-20. He is currently averaging a career-high 3.7 offensive rebounds. -- Marks

19. Washington Wizards

2026-27 record: 4-7
Previous ranking: 16
Next games: @ IND (Nov. 11), vs. DET (Nov. 12), vs. HOU (Nov. 15)

Top newcomer: C Anthony Davis

The 10-time All-Star counts as a newcomer, right? He technically joined the Wizards last February but didn't play a game for them until this season. All he has done with his new team is average 25.7 points and 9.7 rebounds this season. Washington is 4-5 when Davis plays and 0-2 when he doesn't, including a 39-point shellacking in Oklahoma City without the star big man on the court. -- Kram

20. New Orleans Pelicans

2026-27 record: 4-7
Previous ranking: 22
Next games: vs. BKN (Nov. 11), vs. MEM (Nov. 13), vs. DEN (Nov. 14)

Top newcomer: F Trendon Watford

Coach Jamahl Mosley has largely relied on familiar faces while juggling his rotation due to injuries. Believe it or not, New Orleans' top eight scorers are all returning members of last year's 26-win team. Watford, a journeyman forward who joined the Pelicans on a minimum contract this summer, has worked his way into Mosley's rotation by averaging 7.2 points and 3.5 rebounds off the bench over the past six games. Meanwhile, Bennedict Mathurin, a 2022 lottery pick who inked a two-year, $15.4 million deal with New Orleans in free agency, is averaging a career-low 15.0 minutes per game. -- Golliver

21. Phoenix Suns

2026-27 record: 4-6
Previous ranking: 24

2026-27 record: 4-7
Previous ranking: 20
Next games: @ PHX (Nov. 12), @ LAC (Nov. 15), @ LAL (Nov. 17)

Allen is averaging 15.3 points for the Hornets while making 47% of his 3-point tries. Charlotte ranks 28th in 3-point percentage as a team, but that's not Allen's fault. 2026-27 record: 3-7

Da Silva is not considered a newcomer since he was drafted in the 2024 first round. But with the injury to Paolo Banchero, Da Silva is averaging career highs in minutes (30.5) and points (15.1). 2026-27 record: 2-8
Previous ranking: 25
Next games: vs. OKC (Nov. 13), vs. CHA (Nov. 15), vs. UTAH (Nov. 17)

The 6-5 guard, selected with the No. 5 pick out of Illinois, ranks fifth in 3-point percentage (39.0%) among rookies with at least 30 attempts. 26. Brooklyn Nets

2026-27 record: 2-8
Previous ranking: 29
Next games: @ NO (Nov. 11), @ MEM (Nov. 14), vs. PHI (Nov. 16)

Top newcomer: F Julius Randle

It has been hit or miss for Randle so far this season -- he has had bouts of being the most consistent Net on a team full of developing guards. He has had to create his own offense, which he might prefer, as Mikel Brown Jr. and Egor Demin are also battling injuries. He and Michael Porter Jr. can only play together so much because their styles clash, and on some nights like Sunday against Dallas, he'll be a minus-33 in a 130-93 loss. He's a proud veteran in a tough situation -- not an ideal one -- and the Nets have to find ways to maximize him on this ill-fitting team. -- Goodwill

2026-27 record: 1-10
Previous ranking: 26
Next games: vs. ORL (Nov. 11), @ HOU (Nov. 13), vs. SAS (Nov. 15)

After a slow start, Darryn Peterson has started to get cooking, displaying the scoring ability that enticed the Jazz to draft him with the No. 2 pick. 2026-27 record: 1-8
Previous ranking: 27

There haven't been many bright spots for the Bulls so far, but Wilson looks like he belongs. The early returns are strong at 19 points and six rebounds per game, yet his potential is tantalizing. He attacks the basket with intent to dunk everything, and his highlights on defense are eye-popping. Wilson isn't used to losing frequently, so with the Bulls in position to keep racking up L's, Chicago is already trying to manage his body language and effort. Tiago Splitter benched him last week against the Knicks because he noticed him getting down after missing some shots. Still, despite the growing pains, Wilson is easily the team's best newcomer. -- Collier

2026-27 record: 1-10
Previous ranking: 28

He has come out the gates as a great rebounder, and since moving to the starting lineup, he's averaging 13.0 points, eight rebounds and 3.5 assists in 29 minutes. As the Bucks' season continues to slip away, Burries should get even more opportunities. -- Collier

2026-27 record: 1-10
Previous ranking: 30
Next games: vs. POR (Nov. 13), vs. OKC (Nov. 15)

The No. 7 pick has opened his career with 20 or more shot attempts in 10 consecutive games, the longest streak for a rookie since Wilt Chamberlain (19 games) back in 1959. It hasn't all been cloaked in inefficiency, either. Acuff has made 45% or more of those shots in five of the last six games, showing greater comfort and passing willingness. He has games of 10, 12 and 14 assists during that stretch. Acuff recently: "Early on, I wasn't making as many reads. I was forcing a lot of shots. I think the game has slowed down for me." -- Slater

stories.headline: Witnessing Jacob Misiorowski's Cy Young-worthy season
stories.summary: What's it like seeing a Cy Young favorite unleash a 105 mph fastball? We asked those around the Brewers' breakout star.
stories.body:
Editor's note: This story originally ran on Sept. 18. Jacob Misiorowski is a finalist to win the National League Cy Young Award announced on Nov. 11.

Jacob Misiorowski will have to wait until November to see if his first full major league season ends with a National League Cy Young Award, but the Milwaukee Brewers ace is the runaway winner when it comes to oohs and aahs drawn on the mound.

The 24-year-old has thrown 1,053 fastballs over 100 mph this season -- 582 more than anyone else in the sport. Powered by that unparalleled heat, "The Miz" leads the majors with a 1.89 ERA, 0.81 WHIP and 243 strikeouts.

What is it like watching MLB's next great flamethrower dominate the sport? Ahead of his final scheduled start of the 2026 regular season, we asked Misiorowski's teammates what stood out most about his breakout year.

'The velocity jumps out for sure'

Misiorowski joined Jordan Hicks, Aroldis Chapman and Mason Miller as the only four pitchers since pitch tracking began in 2008 to throw 500 or more pitches at 100-plus mph in a single season. But even those three fellow flamethrowers pale in comparison to Miz's total number of triple-digit pitches. Hicks is second on the list with 659 pitches at 100 mph in 2018, but he, Chapman and Miller were able to air it out in short relief stints while Miziorowski has done it in a starting role.

Infielder David Hamilton: "A starter throwing that hard for that long is incredible. I sneak a peek at the board. The velocity jumps out for sure."

Catcher William Contreras: "For some people, watching him pitch that fast is out of this world. Now that I've gone the whole year catching Miz, it's gotten normal for me."

Reliever Chad Patrick: "I got to see him pitch in 2024. He was bringing it then. You start to question when he's throwing 99. Is something wrong? But nothing is wrong. He's doing his thing."

Starter Brandon Woodruff: "I would reference [Jacob] deGrom because he's the closest thing to what he's doing. He's throwing fastballs to one spot, and you see how successful he is. You can do that. Just get it over the plate and you can expand from there."

Outfielder Jackson Chourio: "I start a game thinking I have to be active out there -- but no, you don't."

Outfielder Christian Yelich: "Often they know it's coming. Sometimes they get to it. Most of the time they don't."

'Like a flash'

One pitch stands out from the rest of Miz's blazing heaters this season: A 105.5 mph laser to Chicago Cubs NL MVP candidate Pete Crow-Armstrong on June 26. It's the fastest pitch thrown this year in MLB -- and the fastest ever by a starting pitcher.

Contreras: "That pitch was like a flash. I'm thankful for him being on my team and not another."

Outfielder Garrett Mitchell: "It was electric. Every time he throws, we're expecting something great like that. I looked up [at another pitch] and saw 104. I was like, 'Man, this guy is throwing fuel up there.'"

Woodruff: "It's hard to hit 95, so 105 is really hard. I remember when I was hitting. No thank you."

Hamilton: "I don't know how [Crow-Armstrong] fouled that pitch off. That's the most impressive thing about it."

'That's a dream for a pitcher'

Just as the pitch to PCA stood out most to his teammates, there was one outing that rose above the rest as well: a 94-pitch complete-game masterpiece against the Philadelphia Phillies. The moment which rose above any this year came June 12 against the Phillies. Misiorowski struck out 15 while giving up just one hit in a 6-0 win.

Patrick: "The nine-inning complete game. That's it for me. Best memory."

Contreras: "That's a dream for a pitcher. Only 94 pitches too. One of the best days."

Misiorowski: "I don't know the last time I had a CG. I had a few in the minor leagues, throwing seven innings. Those don't count. That's the first nine-inning complete game. It was the pinnacle, for sure."

Infielder Joey Ortiz: "That game was pure dominance."

Yelich: "Sometimes you get a little laugh or can't believe it look from the hitters, especially when you play teams you don't see much. That happened against Philly."

Chourio: "Whenever he takes the mound, you're in store for a quick game and one that's in our favor. I was very proud of the complete game."

While his teammates have watched in amazement during his starts, those around Misiorowski have also seen how much work has gone on behind the scenes. Pitching coach Chris Hook believes that the effort between outings has fueled Misiorowski's breakout campaign.

"He's gotten so much better at it," Hook said. "When I see the good in the game, it matches what I see in practice. I'm not saying it wasn't important to him. I don't think he knew how important it was to him. Now, you watch his work and the intention is incredible. The intention and attention to detail."

Woodruff credits delivery adjustments that have allowed him to "get the ball over the plate more consistently" and let his most unhittable pitch be unhittable.

"Dude, you have the best fastball in the game," Woodruff recalled saying. "Use that sucker."

That control has helped his walk rate plummet, from 11.4% to 6.6%.

"He's in the zone more this year," Yelich said. "I feel like that was his final hurdle to becoming this kind of pitcher. The way he commands the zone better. The stuff wasn't the question."

Woodruff added: "Young, wiry, long levers. A lot of things playing in his favor. He took last year and learned from it."

What is Misiorowski most proud of (outside of the complete-game shutout)? The moment came recently, from one start to the next -- and both against the rival Cubs. On a hot and humid night at Wrigley Field, Misiorowski gave up five runs in four innings. Six days later, he struck out nine while limiting Chicago to a single run.

"I had a bad one then to bounce back like that was really good," Misiorowski said. "I don't think I would have last year. I would have spiraled and overthought the whole thing, like, 'Oh s---,' I'm facing the same team. That was a big one."

He stopped short of diving into any more memories of the season, knowing that bigger games are still ahead of them. With a division title wrapped up and another potential No. 1 seed in the postseason, Misiorowski and his teammates are hopeful that the biggest and best moments are still ahead.

"I'll look back on it all after the entire season is over," Misiorowski said. "There is still work to be done."

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United add Brentford defender Nathan Collins to shortlist
stories.summary: Brentford center back Nathan Collins has been added to Manchester United's list of defensive options. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Manchester United's list of defensive options now includes Brentford center back Nathan Collins, while Bayern Munich are still in talks to sign Liverpool's teenage winger Rio Ngumoha. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Brentford center back Nathan Collins has been added to Manchester United's list of defensive options for the January transfer window, as reported by The Daily Mail. The Republic of Ireland captain has a contract until 2029, but 8th-placed Brentford would expect a hefty sum to let him go. Only Crystal Palace and Ipswich Town have conceded more Premier League goals this season than the 19 Man United have let in, and Fulham defender Calvin Bassey is also reported to be on the club's shortlist.

- Bayern Munich are still in talks to sign Liverpool's teenage winger Rio Ngumoha, as reported by Bild's Christian Falk. Bayern were willing to pay €70 million to land the 18-year-old during the summer as they looked for a left winger who could complement Luis Díaz, before they went on to sign Ismael Saibari. But Bayern still need a left winger and could still look to land the England international in either January or the summer transfer window.

- Arsenal are eyeing a January move for Real Madrid forward Endrick, according to TalkSPORT. The versatile 20-year-old has played just 114 minutes this season and the Gunners are looking for attacking reinforcements on the wing following Bukayo Saka's injury. The Brazil international is one of a number of options being offered to Premier League clubs, but Diario AS has suggested there will be competition from AS Roma and Sporting CP, who both want to take Endrick on loan.

- In addition to referencing Endrick, The Independent has suggested Arsenal are also looking at Atlético Madrid's Álex Baena, RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa and AFC Bournemouth's Junior Kroupi as they aim to sign a winger. With Real Madrid, Atlético and Chelsea all interested in central midfielder Martín Zubimendi, the Gunners would use the funds from any departure to sign a wide man.

- AC Milan are already making a move for Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi in January and want to pair him with Gonçalo Ramos, as reported by Gazzetta dello Sport. The negotiations are likely to be costly, though, as Brugge rejected a €35 million bid from Roma in the summer and Tresoldi has since gone on to score 13 goals in 15 games across the Jupiler Pro League and Champions League. It is expected that a fee of €50 million would now be required to sign the 22-year-old.

- Internazionale could sign a center back in January if John Stones' injury problems continue. (Gazzetta dello Sport)

stories.headline: Dirk Kuyt leaves Fenerbahce a week after defeating Liverpool
stories.summary: Dirk Kuyt left Fenerbahce on Wednesday, one week after guiding the team as interim coach to beat his old club Liverpool in the Champions League.
stories.body:
ISTANBUL -- Dirk Kuyt left Fenerbahce on Wednesday, one week after guiding the team as interim coach to beat his old club Liverpool in the Champions League.

The former Netherlands forward took charge of that 3-2 win in Istanbul despite the club already having made a deal with Emre Belözoğlu to take over.

Kuyt returned in July to Fenerbahce, where he played from 2012-15, to assist coach Ismail Kartal who resigned last month.

"We thank you from the bottom of our hearts for all that you have contributed to these colors," Fenerbahce said in a social media post announcing Kuyt's exit. "Today we say goodbye to you but your place in this big family will never change."

Belözoğlu, a former captain of the club, takes over a team sixth in the Turkish league and 19th in the 36-team Champions League standings.

Fenerbahce's next Champions League opponent is Shakhtar Donetsk in London on Nov. 25.

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: What to watch in Mammoth-Knights, five other games on Wednesday
stories.summary: Find game previews, betting intel, broadcast information, stats and highlights here.
stories.body:
There are six games on the NHL schedule for Wednesday, including a trio of Metro Division teams facing off against Pacific Division foes, two wild-card hopefuls matching up in Orange County, and a critical clash between the Lightning and Sabres in Buffalo.

But the marquee matchup is Utah Mammoth-Vegas Golden Knights. It's a rematch of the clubs' first-round playoff series this past spring, and a battle between two teams that seem poised to have long postseason runs in 2027.

Read on for a look at what you need to know for each game, including betting info and broadcast details.

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Tampa Bay Lightning at Buffalo Sabres

7 p.m. ET (TNT) | TB -125, O/U: 6.5

With teams approaching the quarter mark of the 2026-27 season, there's more information and smarter projections on how each will finish.

Tampa appears well on its way to earning another postseason slot, while Buffalo has a bit of work to do.

This is the first of four meetings between these teams this season after the duo staged one of the best games of the entire 2025-26 season on March 8. The Sabres' 8-7 win included wild streaks of goals from both teams (and three lead changes), as well as 102 combined penalty minutes.

Will Wednesday's bout be as rough and tumble -- and high-scoring?

New York Rangers at Calgary Flames

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NYR -135, O/U: 5.5

After a 3-1 loss to the Flames' Alberta neighbors in Edmonton on Monday, the Rangers get another chance to leave the province with some points.

The Flames have been better than their humble expectations thus far, entering play Wednesday in fifth place in the Pacific Division. A big part of that has been the power play, which is converting at a 28.6% rate that is fifth in the NHL.

New York has been better than some expected, currently holding the No. 3 seed in the Metro. The Rangers have been aided by a glow-up season by Alexis Lafreniere (18 points in 19 games) and a bounce-back campaign for Adam Fox (22 in 19).

Philadelphia Flyers at Edmonton Oilers

9 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | EDM -218, O/U: 6.5

At the start of this season, this game looked tantalizing; after all, it featured a matchup of two teams that made the playoffs in 2026.

Then the season began, and the results could not look any more different for the clubs.

Edmonton's offensive onslaught has two players leading for NHL Awards, with Connor McDavid threatening to breach the 200-point benchmark by season's end. It sits atop the Pacific, with a 13-3-3 record.

Philadelphia has had issues in all three zones, resulting in a minus-21 goal differential and a 5-10-5 record after winning a playoff round in the spring with largely the same roster.

Can the Flyers mount a serious challenge here or will it be another scorefest for McDavid and his pals?

Utah Mammoth at Vegas Golden Knights

9:30 p.m. ET (TNT) | VGK -125, O/U: 6.5

The Golden Knights sit right behind the Oilers in the Pacific, while the Mammoth have slid down the Central standings following a hot start that had them in first during October.

But beyond the standings, this game should have some juice given how hard the two clubs battled this past spring in the Knights' 4-2 series win in the first round of the playoffs.

Each team is led in scoring by a 2026 U.S. Olympian -- Jack Eichel for the Knights and Clayton Keller for the Mammoth -- who has 24 points. While Vegas has six players who have double-digit points, Utah has seven.

Goal suppression has been a stronger component for the Golden Knights thus far, as the 2.63 goals per game they are allowing is fifth in the NHL, compared with 3.50 per game allowed by the Mammoth (24th).

Can Utah muster something extra for this Western showdown to overcome that deficiency?

Nashville Predators at Anaheim Ducks

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | ANA -148, O/U: 6.5

Another sneaky-fun West Coast game, as both the Predators and Ducks enter this game riding five-game winning streaks -- and in playoff position as play begins Wednesday.

Beyond those similarities, these teams are a study in contrasts, particularly when it comes to the relative ages of their key contributors.

The Preds are led in points by Filip Forsberg (age 32), in goals by Steven Stamkos (36) and in assists by Roman Josi (36).

The Ducks are led in those categories, respectively, by Leo Carlsson (21), Cutter Gauthier (22) and Jackson LaCombe (25).

Does the team with the experienced vets take over, or will it be another one for the youngsters?

Pittsburgh Penguins at San Jose Sharks

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | PIT -125, O/U: 6.5

Pittsburgh enters this contest in Northern California after going 1-1 against the Sharks' SoCal neighbors -- defeating the Kings 5-2 but losing to the Ducks by the same score.

This is the first matchup between the teams this season, and both are in desperate need of points after lackluster starts.

Last season, the Penguins won 3-0 at the Shark Tank on Oct. 18, while the Sharks won an epic thriller -- 6-5 in OT -- on Dec. 13 in Pittsburgh, erasing a four-goal third-period deficit before John Klingberg netted the game winner.

Which type of game will we get this time around?

High-scoring hockey games are a fun watch (for non-goalies). On this date over four decades ago, one of the highest-scoring games of all time occurred -- at least for one team.

The NHL record for goals by one team in a game is 16, set on March 3, 1920, by the Montreal Canadiens against the Quebec Bulldogs. On Nov. 11, 1981, the Minnesota North Stars were one goal shy of that mark, defeating the Winnipeg Jets 15-2.

The 2026 AFL Draft is fast approaching. Marvel Stadium will once more play host to the first round at 7:00pm AEDT on November 19, with the draft recommencing for the second round onwards on November 20.

State of play and players to know
Essendon will be on the clock first, holding the top selection a decade on from the last time it took the number one pick to the AFL Draft. The Dons are expected to first bid on Port Adelaide-tied forward Dougie Cochrane, which will trigger a start-of-second-round compensation pick for the Bombers, Tigers and Eagles.

There are familial lines drawn throughout an exciting 2008-born cohort. Cody Walker is the son of high-flying Blue Andrew and will be headed to Princes Park. Cochrane is the son of former North Melbourne and Port Adelaide midfielder Stuart, though he isn't eligible to either team under the 100-game father-son rule. Instead, he's eligible to join the Power as part of their Next Generation Academy as an Indigenous prospect.

Top-10 riser Sam Gayfer is the nephew of 1990 premiership Pie Mick, and Koby LeCras brings goalkicking pedigree via 2018 premiership uncle Mark.

There will be up to five club-tied talents picked in the first round of the AFL Draft. But that won't necessarily result in an extended first night. Over the past five years the first round has averaged out to 25 selections accounting for father-son and academy bids, but clubs are expecting a number closer to the traditional 18 picks in the final intake of the 18-team competition.

Stricter stipulations around matching bids is at play, with clubs only able to use a maximum of two selections when matching for a club-tied prospect, meaning the selections of Port Adelaide, Carlton, Brisbane and GWS will be absorbed as early bids are matched.

We could see a record number of Indigenous talents picked in the first round. The high-water mark was four in 2005 and 2014, and all of Cochrane, Walker, Caylen Murray (Lions Academy), Toby Krasna and Jake Eime could be taken in the first round in 2026.

Thirteen of the top prospects have already been invited to Marvel Stadium on November 19.

Ethan Drever, Arki Butler and Heath Mellody are all still in contention to be the open pool No. 1 pick, with Harry Van Hattum, Gus Teixeira, Mitch Harris and Ethan Matthews (Giants Academy) rounding out the group on top of draft boards alongside Cochrane and Walker.

Murray, Gayfer, Wil Malady and Leo Steed have also received invites in a sign of club interest on night one.

Around 65 picks are expected to be taken across both nights which would surpass the 60 selections last year.

stories.headline: Ex-San Diego FC forward Cédric Bakambu files fair housing lawsuit
stories.summary: Former San Diego FC forward Cédric Bakambu has filed a housing discrimination lawsuit in federal court.
stories.body:
Former San Diego FC forward Cédric Bakambu has filed a housing discrimination lawsuit in federal court against one real estate firm, two property owners and two real estate agents, according to information contained in the filing.

The lawsuit, a copy of which has been viewed by ESPN, alleges the defendants discriminated against Bakambu and his wife, Anne-Laure Hueber, on the basis of "familial status" by denying them the opportunity rent a house because they had children who would be living with them.

According to the lawsuit, filed in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California, the individuals and entities listed as defendants are property owners JW Wealth and Sheila Nasehi, real estate firm Compass California III and Compass agents Gillian Gillies and Bree Bornstein.

Neither Major League Soccer nor San Diego FC are named as a defendant in the lawsuit.

Bakambu and Hueber are seeking unspecified compensatory, statutory and punitive damages, as well as declaratory and injunctive relief, attorney's fees and costs under the Fair Housing Act, the California Fair Employment and Housing Act and the Unruh Civil Rights Act.

Bakambu signed with San Diego FC back on Sept. 3, and in nine matches for SDFC, he scored four goals with one assist.

In an Instagram post dated Nov. 6, Bakambu, a Congo DR international who played at last summer's World Cup, announced that he would no longer be playing for San Diego, stating, "Some decisions are beyond our control."

A request for comment from a representative for JW Wealth wasn't successful. A request for comment from Compass was also not successful.

ESPN has asked San Diego FC and the league for comment. the MLS players' association declined an ESPN request for comment.

The suit, which was filed on Monday, alleged two instances of discrimination. In the first alleged incident, Bakambu made an offer to rent a 5,679 square-foot house in San Diego, Calif. for a monthly rent of $17,500.

The filing details how Gillies, the agent representing Compass, stated that a pool barrier "would be required due to the age of the children" and asked whether Bakambu would pay an estimated $6,000 to install it if the owner approved.

Alternatives were proposed by Bakambu's broker, Sandra Shebani, including mesh covers and splash alarms.

Gillies responded: "A barrier will need to be installed."

The requirement wasn't mentioned in the property listing.

By Sept. 16, Bakambu made an updated offer that included paying a year's rent in advance, a Pool and Spa Liability Addendum, and an agreement to pay for the barrier.

According to the filing, Compass managing director Melanie Fontana later told Shebani that another applicant that met the lease requirements was under consideration, that Bakambu's offer had been received and that the owner would fund any pool safety measures.

The lawsuit goes on to state that on Sept. 18, 2026, Ms. Shebani raised the fair-housing concern directly with Kathy Mehringer, Compass's Broker of Record and Managing Director of Compliance and Risk Management.

Mehringer responded: "Melanie has explained the process. Compass is not violating any fair housing rules - why would you accuse us of doing so? That is not collaboration."

The filing states that Bakambu's offer was never accepted, and the rental listing was withdrawn from the market after his real estate agent raised fair-housing concerns with Compass management. The suit states that by tying rental conditions to the children and their ages, Bakambu and Hueber were discriminated against.

Later, Bakambu and Hueber sought to rent a 6,300 square-foot house through Compass in Rancho Santa Fe, Calif., and on Oct. 11, 2026, after viewing the property with Bornstein, offered a monthly rent of $23,500.

The filing states: "The offer and follow-up from Ms. Hueber went unanswered even after Plaintiffs observed the home being advertised for $20,000 per month by October 26, 2026."

On Nov. 6, the rental property was taken off the market.

The suit alleges that Compass and Bornstein, its listing agent for the second property, discriminated against Bakambu and Hueber by failing to consider or negotiate their offer because of familial status, and that this was in retaliation for Bakambu and Hueber raising fair-housing concerns regarding negotiations for the first property.

While this was going on, Bakambu's family was forced to remain in temporary housing at his own expense, according to the filing.

The filing reads: "Cédric and Anne allege that this sequence was not [an] ordinary rental negotiation. They were denied equal consideration because their household included five children, and Compass subjected them to further adverse treatment after they asserted their fair-housing rights.

"The consequences were concrete: lost housing opportunities, additional expenses, prolonged housing instability, disruption of efforts to arrange schooling and activities for their children, humiliation, and emotional distress."

stories.headline: Qatar, Abu Dhabi races set to go ahead as F1 rules out Imola backup plan for finale
stories.summary: Formula 1 has told Imola it will not be required to hold a season-ending race, meaning the plan to finish 2026 in Qatar and Abh Dhabi is now set in stone.
stories.body:
Formula 1 has told Imola it will not be required to hold a season-ending race, meaning the plan to finish 2026 in Qatar and Abh Dhabi is now set in stone barring unforeseen circumstances.

F1 had created a backup plan to finish the season in Italy on Dec. 6 in case hostilities resumed in the Middle East after the U.S. midterms.

The Italian circuit had started building grandstands but needed to know whether to commit to full-scale preparations.

On Tuesday, the deadline reported by ESPN last week, F1 has now let Imola know it will not be required.

It means as things stand, F1's season finishes with a triple header of races in Las Vegas on Nov. 21, Qatar on Nov. 29 and Abu Dhabi on Dec. 6.

Formula 1 has repeatedly stressed that it has been in constant communication with governments in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, while also monitoring travel advice from relevant European countries where the sport's 11 teams are based.

F1 was emboldened by the fact that MotoGP, also owned by Liberty Media, last weekend raced without issue in the Qatar circuit hosting F1 at the end of this month.

MotoGP team Yamaha pulled out of that event due to the company's global travel policy.

No F1 team has similar restrictions about travelling to the region.

The Imola news means F1 is full-speed ahead with its original schedule plan.

Sources have told ESPN that the final two races can still be scrapped if there were renewed hostilities in the Middle East.

Sources have confirmed in that instance, without Imola, that would mean the season ending with the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

- McLaren's Piastri splits from ex-F1 driver Webber's management team

- Mercedes new era of dominance? Wolff warns of fight to retain constructors'

- Verstappen's P21 to P2: Red Bull a 'disaster to drive' in São Paulo

From a sporting context, both championships are settled -- Kimi Antonelli won the drivers' championship in Mexico, while Mercedes wrapped up the constructors' in Brazil. However, the constructors' championship is how teams are allocated their prize money and plenty of other teams are fighting for positions lower down.

Sources have told ESPN that F1's commercial agreement with the teams states there must be 22 races minimum in a calendar year, although their commercial agreements with broadcasters will be satisfied at the conclusion Las Vegas' event.

The U.S. and Israeli war in Iran earlier in the year forced F1 to cancel April races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia, although Bahrain paid to reschedule with an event at Malaysian circuit in October.

Despite the rescheduled Bahrain race, were the final two races to be cancelled, F1 would be left with 21 races for the season.

stories.headline: Wings' Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd talk relationship on pod
stories.summary: Azzi Fudd hosted Wings teammate Paige Bueckers on her podcast and the two discussed their relationship, Dallas' season and Fudd's recovery from knee surgery.
stories.body:
Dallas Wings teammates Azzi Fudd and Paige Bueckers, the past two WNBA No. 1 draft picks, spoke on Fudd's podcast Friday about a variety of topics, including a personal life update.

"We're not together anymore; it's been a while," Bueckers said on the "Fudd Around and Find Out" podcast. "[We] share that because everybody [was] like, 'Oh my gosh, they're teammates, how is this going to work?'"

Bueckers and Fudd, who were teammates in college at UConn, said they felt the need to address their relationship status in part because of allegations it factored into the Wings picking Fudd at No. 1 in April. Fudd was chosen over TCU guard Olivia Miles, who went on to be the Rookie of the Year for the Minnesota Lynx. Spain's Awa Fam (Seattle Storm) was taken third, followed by teammates from the 2026 champion UCLA Bruins: Lauren Betts (Washington Mystics), Gabriela Jaquez (Chicago Sky) and Kiki Rice (Toronto Tempo).

Fudd, Fam, Betts and Miles were all No. 1 at different points in ESPN's mock draft in the months before the April draft. Bueckers said her previous relationship with Fudd had no impact on Dallas' decision.

"We were not together before she got drafted," Bueckers said. "She was not drafted because she was my girlfriend. She was drafted because she deserved it. She's an amazing human, an amazing basketball player. And we're still friends, we're still cool.

"We played an entire season together; we're the utmost professionals."

Fudd averaged 13.1 points but was limited to just 30 games after an injury to her right knee led to season-ending arthroscopic surgery in August. She offered an update on her health.

"My offseason's been good," Fudd said. "Lots of rehab, lots of training, lots of on-court workouts, lots of traveling. It's been busy.

"I think there's a lot I can improve on. Especially the iso game; I feel like I'm not too comfortable with that yet. I know I'm capable of doing a little bit more. Watching someone like Paige who is able to create from anywhere ... that's great inspiration for me."

Bueckers averaged 20.9 points, 4.1 rebounds and 5.9 assists, and was named to the All-WNBA second team as Dallas reached the playoffs as the No. 7 seed.

The Wings were eliminated in the first round by the eventual champion Golden State Valkyries. Bueckers said she learned a lot from her first playoff experience and complimented Golden State.

"The Valkyries' defense, I can't explain to you how tough they are," Bueckers said. "They swarm, they send bodies, they trap you, they blitz you, they're so connected. I'm glad I got to have that experience against them to open my eyes to what the playoffs are like -- the physicality, the pressure, the environment.

"And I'm proud of our season. I hated losing; I sat and was pissed about it for like a week. I reached out to [Sue Bird] about it, what was her first playoff experience like. I didn't play as well as I wanted to. But it was my first experience, going against a really good opponent, and I was learning and growing through it all."

Fudd and Bueckers also addressed the Wings' move to the 19,000-seat American Airlines Center in downtown Dallas next season after playing at UT Arlington's College Park Center, which seats over 7,000, since the franchise relocated to Texas in 2016.

"UTA was a vibe; we had a ball, we did our thing there," Bueckers said. "But definitely excited to move into Dallas. New times."

While the change in venue will lead to more eyes on Wings games, the two players said they're hoping for less scrutiny of any on-court behavior.

Both said fans shouldn't read into interactions the two have with each other or their teammates as anything other than normal team behavior. They also said they don't stand for "hate of any kind" or "tearing people down to lift us up."

"We've seen a lot of negativity," Bueckers said. "We've had stuff sent to us, stuff sent to our family, our friends. There's been some crazy things said about us. We still support each other, we're still going to be great friends, we're still going to be great teammates. All the negative things can be put aside, and you don't need to overanalyze everything."

Fudd added with a chuckle, "Also, we don't need messages [from fans] on what the other person's doing. We've addressed everything we need to, and the rest will stay with us."

stories.headline: On the Munny: Cam's new role depends on Walsh groins
stories.summary: Cameron Munster is in a purple patch with his unlikely goalkicking heroics in this World Cup, but whether he continues in the final will depend on Reece Walsh's groins.
stories.body:
Cameron Munster is in a purple patch with his unlikely goalkicking heroics in this World Cup, but whether he continues in the final will depend on Reece Walsh's groins.

The Melbourne magician, a free agent since November 1, said his entire focus was on winning the World Cup and would not be drawn on his club future.

Sunday's final at Suncorp Stadium is expected to be a close contest with goalkicking possibly deciding the outcome, considering the Kiwis have the game's best marksman in Jamayne Isaako.

Munster has barely kicked for Melbourne in the past four years but has been nailing them like Hazem El Masri in his pomp with 11 goals from 15 shots with many of the attempts from the sideline.

He took over from Walsh in the 66-6 win over Cook Islands and continued in the 44-12 victory over Samoa in last week's semi-final.

With regular NRL goalkickers Sam Walker and Latrell Mitchell not in the starting side, the duties have fallen to Munster and he has done a great job despite admitting he does not practise.

"To be completely honest, I don't really like goalkicking," Munster grinned.

"I just do it because we've got no one in our squad doing it at the moment.

"Reece is our number one kicker, so if he feels good enough to do it on Sunday, he'll take over.

"If he pulls up a little bit lame on captain's run with his groins, I'll probably take over."

Munster had one of his best games this year in the semi-final win over Samoa where he ran the ball superbly and was a real handful.

His 18 runs was the most for any Kangaroo and throw in his 146m and three try assists it is a positive sign for the hosts.

"When I am playing my best, it is when I'm running the ball. That's the mindset and the aim for myself on Sunday," Munster said.

"The game might not be the same against New Zealand. I'm sure they've got a plan around myself and I'm sure I'll have to try and figure out a way to get around it."

Munster made his Test debut for Australia in the 2017 World Cup when he played two pool games at centre and halfback. He did not play in the 6-0 win over England in the final, but was No.6 in Australia's 30-10 triumph over Samoa in the 2022 World Cup final.

He has dared to dream about backing that up but said the process and not the outcome was on his mind as he attempts to enure the new players in the side get the satisfaction.

"I remember one of the boys, Jack Bostock, asked me the other day what it was like to win a cup," he said.

"It's something I've been very fortunate enough to be able to win, but these guys who have only just had their first World Cup, you try to give them that taste.

"You never know, four years' time, who's going to be able to be in the squad again."

Munster said in a previous interview he would delay travelling to Papua New Guinea until a later date after postponing a planned visit to talk to PNG Chiefs before November 1 that had been approved by the Storm.

Whether he will head to Port Moresby in future was not a subject he wanted to address on Wednesday.

"I am just focused on the World Cup," Munster said.

"My manager's dealing with all that sort of stuff and once the back end of this World Cup's done ... he'll sort that out, whether that's an option. If not, then it's not."

stories.headline: Jacksonville Jaguars' Foyesade Oluokun leads the way again in Africa's Week 9 NFL exploits
stories.summary: Foyesade Oluokun - a seasoned linebacker of Nigerian heritage - had yet another superb week in Week 9, starring for the Jacksonville Jaguars as they beat the Baltimore Ravens to go 6-2 for the NFL season.
stories.body:
Foyesade Oluokun - a seasoned linebacker of Nigerian heritage - had yet another superb week in Week 9, starring for the Jacksonville Jaguars as they beat the Baltimore Ravens to go 6-2 for the NFL season.

He continues to stand out among Africa's stars in the NFL, and there were several other stars with Nigerian ties across who also had strong performances this week - particularly defensively. Additionally, Zimbabwe's Nate Landman made big plays in the LA Rams' win over the Washington Commanders.

Africa Player of the Week: Foyesade Oluokun (Jacksonville Jaguars)

Oluokun picks up Africa Player of the Week honors for a second successive week after making seven tackles - six of them solo - and a sack in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens.

Oluokun sacked Joe Fagano early in the second quarter, resulting in a two-yard loss for the Ravens on third down. The Jags already led 10-3 by then, but the Ravens were looking to get a drive going to enable them to nullify that advantage, and Oluokun knocked the wind out of their sails.

As usual, however, Oluokun's contribution throughout the win was not built on having the flashiest moments, but rather ruthless consistency and efficiency.

The first-generation Nigerian-American has now made two sacks and two interceptions this season. He is one of only two players in the entire league to have recorded both multiple sacks and multiple interceptions - with the other being the Carolina Panthers' Devin Lloyd.

Africa Moment of the Week: Nick Emmanwori (Seattle Seahawks)

Emmanwori - a safety who is reportedly the youngest of five brothers born to Nigerian parents and raised the country's flag after winning the Super Bowl last season - stopped a touchdown in the 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals.

With just over four and a half minutes left in the fourth quarter, he forced Trey McBride to spill the ball at a crucial moment - keeping the 14-point lead intact.

By defending Gardner Minshew's pass to McBride on fourth down, Emmanwori allowed the Seahawks to start again from their own one-yard line, and they saw out the game from there.

That one-on-one wins Moment of the Week because it was not only a moment of instinctive brilliance from Emmanwori, but also a potentially crucial one in determining which way the game went.

The Seahawks are now 5-4 for the season and despite not being as consistent as last season, they remain in contention.

Honorable mentions

Among other stars of traceable Nigerian descent: Malik Mustapha made an impressive interception for the San Francisco 49ers in their 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, Tyler Onyedim forced a fumble for the Denver Broncos in their 26-21 win over the Carolina Panthers, and Rome Odunze scored his first touchdown of the season as the Chicago Bears beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 27-24.

Emmett Johnson, who has family roots in Liberia, scored a touchdown for the Kansas City Chiefs in a 35-12 win over the New York Jets.

There were players with African ties who made big plays in week 9 but ultimately ended up losing. For one, Austin Ajiake (ties to Nigeria) forced a fumble for the Indianapolis Colts in their 27-23 loss to the Dallas Cowboys.

His compatriot, Josh Uche, made some big plays for the Miami Dolphins in a 19-9 loss to the Detroit Lions with a sack and a pass defended. Another, Ifeatu Melifonwu, had a pass defended and a fumble reception in the Buccaneers' loss to the Bears.

Africa-born Player Watch

Nate Landman - a linebacker born in Harare, Zimbabwe - was the standout African-born player in week 9. He picked up his third forced fumble of the season and is now joint-fifth in the NFL in that department, also notching up a second pass defended for 2026.

Landman had brilliant moments throughout the game, but was not as consistent as Oluokun. While they both ended with seven tackles, Oluokun had six solo and Landman only three.

Most importantly for Landman, however, his Rams picked up a second successive win - beating the Washington Commanders 20-13.
